stories.label: Sudan drone strikes kill 160+; Oil hits five-month high; Mahmoud Khalil appeals to SCOTUS
stories.summary: Write only the Sudan item from this roundup: drone strikes that killed more than 160 people. Lead with the toll, where the strikes hit and who the dead were, then name who is credited with the strikes (RSF or the army) and which outside states supply the drones. The structural point: drone warfare has turned Sudan's war into one where civilians far from any front line die in the dozens, while the world's attention sits on the Gulf. Ignore the oil and Khalil items. Dateline the Sudanese city that was struck.

stories.label: New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
stories.summary: The EU's new Arctic strategy pledges satellite surveillance, icebreaker capacity and protection of undersea cables, and names not only Russia but the United States as a pressure on the region, after Washington's push over Greenland. Lead with that shift: Brussels now plans for an ally as a risk. The mechanism: melting ice opens shipping routes and seabed resources, and Denmark's sovereignty over Greenland makes the EU a party. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Brazil's Farm Lobby Will Gain Even More Power If Bolsonaro Wins
stories.summary: New since yesterday's Meta story: polls now show Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a statistical tie five days before Sunday's runoff, after a million people marched for Lula in São Paulo on 18 October. Lead with what is at stake beyond the two men: the agribusiness caucus, already the strongest bloc in Congress, would gain more power over one of the world's biggest food exporters, with consequences for Amazon deforestation, Indigenous land and pesticide rules. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Departamento de Estado dos EUA financia ONG que questiona liberdade de expressão no Brasil
stories.summary: Agência Pública found the US State Department paid R$150,000 to Instituto Sivis, a Brazilian NGO whose work questions the state of free expression in Brazil, the argument Washington and Brazil's right have used against the Supreme Court's rulings on platforms. Lead with the grant and its timing, days before Sunday's runoff, and give Sivis's denial of foreign interference. The mechanism: a foreign government funding a domestic voice in a fight over platform regulation. Dateline São Paulo.

stories.label: New Data Reveals How Trump 2.0 is Exploiting Asylum Court
stories.summary: In-absentia removal orders in US immigration courts have nearly tripled since early 2025, and the data show many asylum seekers had their hearings moved without knowing it. Lead with the number. The mechanism: rescheduling a hearing without effective notice turns a missed date into a deportation order, with no hearing of the asylum claim at all. Say who holds the power (the Justice Department's immigration courts) and who bears it. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: France's growing debt woes: How bond markets set countries' borrowing costs
stories.summary: French government bond yields have risen to their highest in nearly a quarter century as the worst social unrest in decades (the student-led protests, curfews and a Paris protest ban) collides with a debt investors doubt Paris can control. Lead with the yield and the widening gap over German bonds. The mechanism: markets charge more when a government looks unable to pass a budget, and that premium lands on French taxpayers and the euro. Note that the US and Japan owe more. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Elice's weak debut fuels AI concerns as oil prices climb
stories.summary: South Korean data-centre company Elice fell on its stock market debut, deepening investor doubt that AI infrastructure spending will pay back, as Asian chip stocks tumbled and Brent crude topped $111 a barrel. Lead with the IPO's fall, then the two pressures meeting: costlier energy for power-hungry data centres and doubts about AI returns, which also weigh on chipmakers like AMD. Name Brent crude as the series. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Coega Steels launches R500m low-emission rolling mill, creating 600 jobs
stories.summary: A R500m low-emission rolling mill in Nelson Mandela Bay will create 300 direct and 300 indirect jobs in the Eastern Cape, where unemployment is 47.5%. Lead with that ratio. The structural why: South Africa's steel industry has been shedding plants under high power costs and cheap imports, so a new mill built on lower emissions tests whether green steel can keep industrial jobs at home. Dateline Gqeberha.

stories.label: Vast new fossil record challenges story of Earth's 'big five' mass extinctions
stories.summary: Palaeontologists trained a language-model-style system on fossil records instead of words and used it to reconstruct a far larger record of life's history, which challenges the textbook account of five mass extinctions. Lead with what the new record shows about the 'big five' (fewer, more, or differently timed). Explain the method plainly: the model fills gaps in where and when species appear. Say what it means for judging today's extinction rate.

stories.label: Space probes decode solar eruptions near their origins
stories.summary: Two spacecraft flying close together near the Sun gave unprecedented detail of coronal mass ejections, each hurling about a billion tonnes of material at hundreds of kilometres a second; Indian researchers (Nature India) led the work. Lead with what was seen near the origin that could not be seen from Earth. Why it matters: CMEs knock out satellites and power grids, and earlier warning depends on understanding how they start. Dateline the Indian institute behind the study.

stories.label: Q&A: Why a pivotal IPCC meeting in Ethiopia ended in ‘profound disappointment’
stories.summary: For the sixth time running, governments at the IPCC failed to agree when its next assessment reports will be published. Lead with what this delays: whether the science arrives in time for the 2028 global stocktake. Name which countries blocked agreement and why: a later report weakens the evidence base for tougher emissions targets. Dateline Addis Ababa.

stories.label: Meta ordered to name execs who approved torrenting for AI training
stories.summary: After weeks of blaming staff for torrenting pirated books from Anna's Archive and LibGen to train its AI, Meta has been ordered by a US court to name the executives who authorised it. Lead with the order. Accountability is the point: discovery moves the question from rogue employees to company decision-makers, which matters for wilful-infringement damages and for every AI firm that trained on shadow libraries. Dateline San Francisco.

stories.label: DHS Said They Searched Man Who Wiped GrapheneOS Phone for Child Abuse Material. They Lied
stories.summary: Documents obtained by 404 Media show DHS officials claimed they wanted to search Stop Cop City activist Samuel Tunick's phone for child abuse material, when the real reason was suspected 'terrorist activities'. Lead with the gap between the stated and real reason. The mechanism: border-search powers and a child-abuse pretext let agents get past an activist's encryption without a warrant, and Tunick now faces charges for wiping his GrapheneOS phone. Dateline Atlanta.

stories.label: Space Rider Test Model Lost Following Failed Drop Test
stories.summary: A full-scale test model of ESA's Space Rider, Europe's reusable uncrewed spaceplane, was lost when its parafoil failed to deploy: the second drop-test anomaly this year after May's aborted attempt. Lead with the loss. The structural why: Space Rider is Europe's bid for its own return-capable orbital vehicle while it still depends on SpaceX for much of its access to space, and another delay widens that gap. Dateline at the test site named in the report.

stories.label: Huge setback for Alberta's separatist movement after decisive defeat
stories.summary: The result of yesterday's vote, which we previewed: with over 1.5 million ballots counted, 76% of Albertans voted to stay in Canada and about 24% to start a path toward separation. Lead with the margin. The mechanism: an oil province's grievance over federal climate and pipeline policy was turned into a sovereignty question and lost decisively, a win for Carney and a blow to Premier Danielle Smith, who allowed the vote. Say what the referendum would have triggered (a process, not independence) and what it means for Saskatchewan's separatists. Dateline Edmonton.

stories.label: The UK expands military support for Saudi Arabia against Houthis to include 'de...
stories.summary: Britain will deploy RAF Typhoon jets to fly defensive air patrols over Saudi Arabia against Houthi missiles and drones, and says they will not strike the group. Lead with a European power stepping into the Saudi–Houthi front after strikes on Riyadh's airport and Aramco's Dhahran headquarters. The mechanism: the 'defensive only' line keeps London out of the war on paper while it guards the kingdom's oil and airports; set it beside Turkey, Pakistan and Egypt's own 'defence only' pledges. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: AfD Leak: What 421,179 Hacked Emails Show about the German Far Right
stories.summary: A trove of 421,179 hacked emails from Germany's AfD, the far-right party now leading or near the top of national polls. Lead with the single most concrete finding the source documents: who was in contact with whom, what money or policy the emails show. Attribute every claim to the leaked emails as analysed by the outlet, and say what has and has not been verified. Mechanism: what the internal record shows about how the party is run, set against what it says in public. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: Envoy says Iraq agrees to expel anti-Iran terrorist group
stories.summary: Iran's ambassador in Baghdad, Mohammad Kazem Al-e-Sadeq, says Iraq has agreed to expel an Iranian Kurdish separatist group from the Kurdistan Region. This rests on Iranian state media alone: write 'Iran's state-run Mehr News Agency reported' and do not state the agreement as fact. Mechanism: with the US-Iran war in its eighth month, Tehran is pressing Baghdad to clear Iranian Kurdish exile groups from the Kurdistan Region; name the people who would be displaced and say Baghdad and Erbil have not confirmed it if the source shows no confirmation. Dateline Baghdad.

stories.label: Qatar is ramping up liquefied natural gas exports as prices surge
stories.summary: Qatar is pushing more LNG out as European gas prices surge before winter: at least 20 cargoes have passed through the Strait of Hormuz, and one tanker bound for Poland is taking the rare Red Sea route past the Houthis. Lead with that tanker. Mechanism: the war has made both chokepoints dangerous, so every Qatari cargo is a bet on which strait stays open, and Europe's winter heating rides on it. Name natural gas prices and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Dateline Doha.

stories.label: Google says 'multiple' Cloud services suffer network failures in Europe
stories.summary: A power event at Google Cloud's London data centre knocked out multiple services, disrupting Revolut, other UK banks and the courts. Lead with who went dark: banks and courts that run on one provider's single region. Mechanism: concentration risk, where a fault in one building becomes a failure across finance and public services; say what regulators require of banks on cloud resilience. Dateline London.

stories.label: Macron secures 200,000 tonnes of extra diesel per month from UAE, Bahrain
stories.summary: Macron, touring Gulf suppliers, secured an extra 200,000 tonnes of diesel a month from the UAE and Bahrain. Lead with the number and why France needs it: fuel costs are part of what put France's streets into its worst unrest in decades. Mechanism: a European president bargaining for fuel in the middle of a war that has closed or endangered the Gulf's sea lanes; say how the cargoes reach France and what share of French diesel demand the deal covers. Name Brent crude. Dateline Abu Dhabi.

stories.label: India-New Zealand FTA kicks in, promises 'more jobs and higher wages' for Kiwis
stories.summary: The India–New Zealand free trade agreement is now in force, with duty-free access for Indian goods. Lead with what changed today: which tariffs fell and on what (textiles, leather, farm goods). Mechanism: India has long kept dairy out of every trade deal to protect its smallholders; say whether dairy was carved out here and who on each side gains or loses. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: 梁圣大气！DeepSeek推理框架全开源，公布日均吞吐和毛利，真正的OpenAI来了
stories.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its V4.1 Flash service, which runs on both Nvidia and Huawei Ascend chips, and disclosed its economics: one cluster serves 155 trillion tokens a day and earns about $38 per card per hour. Lead with those disclosed numbers, which no US lab publishes. Mechanism: open-sourcing the serving stack, not just the weights, lets any provider match DeepSeek's prices, and running on Ascend narrows the reach of US chip controls; tie it to the MiniMax–DeepSeek price war. Dateline Hangzhou.

stories.label: Meta Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
stories.summary: Researchers found that conversations users share by link from Meta's new Muse AI agent are publicly searchable: one query lists thousands by title, exposing personal and business secrets. Lead with the single query. Mechanism: a 'share' link treated as private by users but indexable by design, the same failure that hit ChatGPT shared chats; say what Meta has done since the report.

stories.label: FAQ: Was man zum Verhaltensscanner in Berlin wissen sollte
stories.summary: Berlin police are switching on software that scores the behaviour of people filmed by cameras, starting at Kottbusser Tor, a square in Kreuzberg with a large Turkish and Arab population. Lead with the first camera going live. Mechanism: the software flags 'abnormal' movement for officers rather than identifying faces; say what legal basis Berlin uses, what counts as suspicious behaviour, and who decided which neighbourhood came first. Dateline Berlin.

stories.label: ‘Reverse-Engineer Anything’ Is the New Wild West of AI
stories.summary: AI models are now decompiling, cloning and modifying closed software on request, and the results are going viral. Lead with the most concrete case in the source (a product cloned or a device unlocked). Mechanism: decompilation used to take a skilled engineer weeks; now it costs a prompt, which undercuts both software copyright and the 'security through obscurity' that much hardware relies on. Fold in 404's companion report on hobbyists using AI decompiling to hack their own devices.

stories.label: Scientists Discover A Strange Particle Explains the Origin of Reality
stories.summary: Physicists propose that a long-overlooked particle may have tipped the balance toward matter over antimatter in the first instants after the Big Bang, one of physics' great open questions. Lead with the particle and the paper behind it (journal and team). Be precise about status: a proposal or calculation, not an observation, unless the source says otherwise; say what experiment could test it.

stories.label: South Korea to pull more embassy staff from Ukraine after POW row
stories.summary: Seoul is withdrawing more embassy staff from Kyiv after recalling its ambassador, because Ukraine gave no 'constructive response' over North Korean prisoners of war it disclosed transferring. Lead with the escalation. The why: captured North Korean soldiers are a legal and humanitarian question (South Korea's constitution treats them as its citizens, and they face punishment if returned to Pyongyang), and the row shows the Russia war pulling the Korean peninsula into Europe's conflict. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: Dar, other delegates welcomed in Dushanbe ahead of SCO meeting
stories.summary: At the SCO heads-of-government meeting in Dushanbe, India's Rajnath Singh said there can be 'no double standards' on terrorism with Pakistan's Ishaq Dar in the room. Lead with India and Pakistan sparring inside a China- and Russia-led bloc, using the two outlets' opposite framings (sentiment divergence is high). Second beat: Russian PM Mishustin said most settlements between SCO members are now in national currencies, up from about half five years ago (TASS; attribute) — the bloc's slow move off the dollar. Dateline Dushanbe.

stories.label: Rubio arrives in India amid growing pressure on global energy markets
stories.summary: After Samarkand, Rubio lands in Mumbai with a large business delegation to reset ties strained by US tariffs and India's purchases of Russian oil, while the Gulf war squeezes India's energy imports. Lead with what Washington wants (less Russian crude, more US energy and arms purchases) and what India wants (tariff relief). The mechanism: India's oil import bill under Brent above $110 gives Washington leverage it did not have last year. Dateline Mumbai.

stories.label: Ukraine, US to hold Norway peace talks as Zelensky, Trump tension grows
stories.summary: Zelensky, US envoy Steve Witkoff and the leaders of Norway and Finland meet in Oslo as Washington presses Kyiv for concessions to reach a deal with Russia. Lead with the pressure: what territorial or security concessions the US is asking for, days after Putin floated a Trump–Xi summit on Ukraine and Russia knocked out power to 550,000 households. Note who is not at the table — Russia and Ukraine's other European backers. Dateline Oslo.

stories.label: Hegseth meets Netanyahu in unannounced Israel visit
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made an undisclosed visit to Israel to meet Netanyahu ahead of a closely contested election (Axios first reported it). Lead with the timing: a Pentagon chief appearing beside a prime minister weeks before a vote, while the US fights Iran and Gaza remains under Israeli control behind the yellow line. Say what was on the table (Iran, munitions) and that a US visit is itself a campaign asset. Dateline Jerusalem.

stories.label: ‘Dark Horse da Shopee’: 2º filme sobre Bolsonaro teve convite a Vorcaro e é alvo da Ancine
stories.summary: An Agência Pública investigation: a second film about Bolsonaro declared a cost of only R$4,500, invited banker Daniel Vorcaro (Banco Master) and is under review by the film agency Ancine over whether it was paid for with parliamentary amendment money. Lead with the implausible declared budget. Accountability angle days before the runoff in which Flávio Bolsonaro faces Lula: who financed the film and whether public money paid for campaign propaganda. Dateline São Paulo.

stories.label: Two oil tankers on fire after hitting mine in Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: New development: the IRGC says two more 'violating' tankers hit mines and caught fire on an 'illegal route' south of the Strait of Hormuz, and that it downed a US MQ-9 drone overnight — one day after a single tanker hit a mine. Iranian state news agency Mehr reports it; attribute every claim and do not state it as fact. Lead with the two tankers against Iran's six-day reopening offer and Qatar's statement that US–Iran talks continue. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude, now above $111.

stories.label: Asian refiners use smaller tankers, buy delivered crude as freight rates soar
stories.summary: With tanker spot rates near records because of the Gulf war, Asian refiners are switching to smaller ships, long-term charters and buying Middle East crude on a delivered basis to push freight risk onto sellers. Lead with the freight number and what it adds per barrel. The mechanism: war-risk insurance and a shrinking fleet willing to sail the Gulf make shipping, not crude, the cost that lands on Asian importers and their fuel buyers. Name the series: Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Dateline Singapore.

stories.label: Russian Satellite’s Unprecedented Shadowing Of A Very Particular Radar Imaging Satellite Is A Big Deal
stories.summary: Russia's Kosmos 2612 manoeuvred for weeks to come very close to ICEYE X36, a commercial radar-imaging satellite from the Finnish firm reportedly tied to Ukraine's battlefield intelligence. Lead with the closest approach. The why: commercial satellites now supply a warring state's targeting, which makes a private company's spacecraft a military target, and a co-orbital inspector is the step before jamming or interference. Dateline Helsinki.

stories.label: Defense contractors in two NATO allies hacked in recent Russia-linked campaign
stories.summary: Researchers say Russia's APT28 (Fancy Bear) used a recently documented backdoor to sit inside the networks of two defence contractors and a law-enforcement agency in two NATO countries. Lead with how long they dwelt and what the backdoor does. The why: the same military-intelligence unit is mapping Europe's arms supply to Ukraine, alongside the sabotage campaign such as the Lithuanian Starlink arson. Name the countries and the research firm. Dateline where the researchers place the victims.

stories.label: Near miss: Indonesia probes crash of suspected Chinese rocket fragment
stories.summary: A car-sized piece of debris, possibly from a Chinese rocket according to an Indonesian government agency, crashed into a palm oil plantation near homes and work sites. Lead with how close it came to people. The mechanism: uncontrolled re-entry of spent rocket stages, a practice China has been criticised for, leaves the risk with whoever lives under the flight path, and the Outer Space Liability Convention makes the launching state liable. Dateline at the crash site if named, otherwise Jakarta.

stories.label: Kenyan pastor convicted for ordering 191 followers to starve to death
stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie and 28 other leaders of his Shakahola cult were convicted of murdering 191 people, 190 of them children, starved on his orders to 'meet Jesus'. Lead with the 190 children. The structural why: police and local officials had complaints about Mackenzie years before the bodies were exhumed in the Shakahola forest near Malindi, and the verdict is the first accounting for a state that let the starvation run.

stories.label: The world was talking about him being dead! Kim Jong-un appeared
stories.summary: Seoul's Defence Ministry vowed 'resolute punishment' if Pyongyang acts on threats to harden its military posture along the border, the same day North Korean state media released photos of Kim Jong Un at a clothing expo after days of brain-haemorrhage and death rumours. Lead with the border threat, not the rumour: what Pyongyang says it will do at the line, and why a leader proving he is alive pairs with a show of force.

stories.label: Colombia illegal gold mine collapse kills 14 people
stories.summary: A landslide at an illegal gold mine in Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé, Nariño, killed 14 and injured 7. The why: gold at record prices pulls workers into unregulated pits in a department where armed groups control the mining economy, and the state is present only after the bodies are counted. Lead with the toll, then name who profits from the gold and who digs it.

stories.label: Saudi Arabia cancels 2026 'Davos in the Desert' amid Houthi attacks
stories.summary: Riyadh postponed the Future Investment Initiative, its flagship pitch to global capital, to 2027 after deadly Houthi attacks on the kingdom. Lead with what the cancellation concedes: the war has reached the investment case behind Vision 2030. Continues the Gulf war arc after the Houthi strike that killed 18 in Shabwa.

stories.label: Persian Gulf authority acts against 40 violating vessels
stories.summary: Iran's new Persian Gulf Strait Authority says it has acted against more than 40 vessels and put 122 on a non-compliance list, Iran's state agency Mehr reported — Tehran running the Strait of Hormuz as a permit regime. Bloomberg reports WTI near $98 as traders weigh Iranian threats against still-robust Gulf crude flows. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; attribute the PGSA figures to Mehr.

stories.label: Micron union in Taiwan to launch strike as bonus dispute escalates
stories.summary: A union of Micron workers in Taoyuan will strike Thursday, timed to a mediation meeting for its Taichung staff, over bonuses in a memory boom driven by AI servers. Lead with the leverage: Taiwan's fabs make much of Micron's DRAM, and the workers want a share of the windfall. Micron shares fell 8.5% last week; say what the strike puts at risk, not why the stock moved.

stories.label: NZ's climate in 'uncharted territory,' with more extreme weather events ahead
stories.summary: A major new assessment finds New Zealand's climate has warmed into 'uncharted territory', as a record-strength El Niño forms on top of that baseline. Lead with the assessment's measured findings, not the El Niño forecast: what has shifted, by how much, and what the record El Niño does to a drier, windier north and east.

stories.label: Arrested OpenAI Employee Was Asked To Join Saudi Arabia's AI Effort, US Alleges
stories.summary: US prosecutors allege the ex-OpenAI engineer accused of planting a recording device in an executive conference room was in frequent contact with an unnamed Saudi royal and was asked to join the kingdom's AI effort. Lead with the device in the conference room, then the mechanism: Gulf money racing to buy frontier-AI capability, and what prosecutors have and have not shown about state direction.

stories.label: 字节Seed大重组：吴永辉的“大兵团”作战，与出走的联合创始人
stories.summary: ByteDance has restructured Seed, its large-model research unit, under Wu Yonghui into a 'large-army' operation to industrialise model development, while a co-founder has left. Lead with what the reorganisation changes in how China's biggest-spending AI lab builds models, read from the mainland tech press's own reporting, and who walked out.

stories.label: Israeli opposition slams Netanyahu's new security doctrine as 'empty slogans' ahead of elections
stories.summary: Eight days before the 27 October election, Netanyahu, who is wanted by the ICC, unveiled a national security doctrine and a map that sorts the region into rival blocs. Eisenkot and Lapid call it hollow campaigning. Lead with what the doctrine commits Israel to (permanent forward presence, its stance on Iran and the 'alliances' map) and who is cast as an enemy. The Polymarket contract on the election swung sharply this week, so this is a live race: say what the doctrine is meant to win at the ballot box. Dateline Jerusalem.

stories.label: Residents winched from rooftops as torrential rain hits eastern Spain
stories.summary: Floods and storms killed at least three people in the Valencia region, helicopters winched people from rooftops, and more than 80,000 residents were ordered to shelter in place. The same coast lost over 220 people in the October 2024 DANA, when the regional alert reached phones only after the water had arrived. Lead with the toll and the shelter order, then the accountability question: did the warning system rebuilt after 2024 work this time? Dateline Valencia.

stories.label: Yemen forces advance in Taiz; Iran blames US for Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: Government and Saudi-backed forces are advancing on Houthi lines around Taiz, a city under siege for a decade, opening a new ground front as the Saudi–Houthi war widens after the Shabwa camp strike. Lead with the Taiz advance: where the lines moved and what it means for the civilians still under siege there. Mention briefly Araghchi blaming Washington for the Hormuz crisis (Reuters). Hormuz itself was covered this cycle, so keep it secondary. Dateline Taiz.

stories.label: Search under way for four soldiers missing after gang attack in Haiti
stories.summary: Gangs blew up an armoured vehicle of the UN-backed force near Croix-des-Bouquets, and four Salvadoran soldiers are missing, as the Security Council meets on Haiti. Lead with the ambush and the missing soldiers. The structural point: the gangs can now hit the international force's armour directly, and Haitians in the areas they control remain without protection. Dateline Port-au-Prince.

stories.label: In NA, Achakzai demands to know Sohail Afridi's whereabouts
stories.summary: The elected chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sohail Afridi of PTI, has not been seen since his government became non-functional under president's rule. The opposition leader, Mehmood Khan Achakzai, demanded on the floor of the National Assembly that the state say where he is. Lead with that: a sitting provincial head of government whose whereabouts are unknown. Explain how president's rule sidelined an elected provincial government, and who in Islamabad and Rawalpindi holds the answer. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: De la Espriella resets relations between Colombia and Israel
stories.summary: Colombia, which under Petro cut ties with Israel over Gaza, has become only the tenth country to move its embassy to Jerusalem, under its new president, Abelardo de la Espriella. Lead with the reversal, from a Gaza-driven break to recognising Jerusalem, and what it signals: a shift in Latin America's right-wing governments, and a recognition that runs against international law on occupied East Jerusalem. Dateline Bogotá.

stories.label: US allowing 'dark fleet' oil tankers to ship crude, Energy Secretary says | The National
stories.summary: New development on the Russia sanctions waiver: Energy Secretary Chris Wright says Washington is now letting sanctioned 'dark fleet' tankers start a process to ship crude legitimately, while denying that this lifts sanctions. Meanwhile Trump faces bipartisan blowback in Congress over the waiver he signed two days before new sanctions took effect (Semafor, Aol, TRT World), and said what Russia is doing to Ukraine is 'fine' (Kyiv Independent). Lead with the dark-fleet decision and who gains: Moscow's oil revenue while it strikes Ukraine's grid. Name Brent crude, which is near $110 on the Gulf war. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Nscale, Anthropic in Talks for $45 Billion Cloud Computing Deal
stories.summary: Hours after we reported that Nscale lost its Microsoft AI data-centre deal because the UK grid connection slips into the 2030s, the Nvidia-backed firm is in talks to sell Anthropic about $45 billion of computing power. Lead with that turn. The mechanism: frontier labs are pre-buying compute years ahead, so a developer can swap one tenant for another, but grid capacity, not chips, still decides when any of it runs. Dateline London.

stories.label: Digital gold market triples to $55bn as younger investors pile in
stories.summary: A World Gold Council survey puts tokenised gold holdings at 370 tonnes, and the digital gold market has tripled since early 2025 to as much as $55bn as younger investors buy fractional bullion. Lead with the 370 tonnes, more than many central banks hold. The mechanism: a war-driven gold boom is moving into tokens. Raise the custody question: who holds the metal behind each token? For a Muslim reader, note that tokenised gold raises the old question of whether a gold trade is hand-to-hand. Chart gold. Dateline London.

stories.label: Explainer: What is Africa Bitcoin Corporation and why did it make the FSCA mad?
stories.summary: Daily Maverick read 251 documents to show that Africa Bitcoin Corporation, the former Altvest Capital, has little to do with bitcoin and has drawn action from South Africa's Financial Sector Conduct Authority. Lead with what the regulator objected to and what retail shareholders actually own. The accountability angle: a listed company rebranded around a crypto treasury story while the regulator moved in. Dateline Johannesburg.

stories.label: Anthropic exposes AI operation that DRC journalists never knew existed
stories.summary: Seventy AI-run fake news sites published 318 articles on the eastern Congo war, relations with Rwanda and contested minerals, and Congolese journalists learned of it only from an Anthropic threat report. Lead with 70 sites and 318 articles. The point: the information war over Congo's minerals now runs on AI content farms, and local newsrooms cannot see them. Name who the operation favoured, if the report says. Dateline Goma.

stories.label: A eleição das Big Techs
stories.summary: Days before Sunday's Brazilian runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, Agência Pública reports Meta blocking pro-Lula and anti-Flávio political posts as 'terrorism' and 'nudity'. Lead with the concrete moderation cases and who they hit. The structural point: platform content moderation is shaping the last week of a national election in a country that has fought the tech platforms in court. Dateline São Paulo.

stories.label: 'It Ain't Right:' Texas Said It Would Halt Data Center Permits. The State is Pushing Ahead Anyway
stories.summary: Texas announced a pause on data-centre permits, yet the Stargate site, Caldwell Technology Park and other hyperscale campuses keep getting approvals. Lead with the gap between the announced halt and the permits still issued. Who pays: residents facing grid strain and water draw from facilities the state says it paused. Dateline Austin.

stories.label: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in "proof point" test
stories.summary: The first demonstration of a subsea geothermal power plant, at an active underwater volcano nearly a mile down, produced net-positive electricity for under 10 seconds. Lead with that honest number: a proof of physics, not of a power station. The why: Pacific Rim nations that import their oil sit on submarine hydrothermal systems, and this tests whether that heat can be harvested. Say what has to scale before it matters.

stories.label: Beehives act as 'living immune systems' with layered antimicrobial defenses
stories.summary: Researchers found that honeybee hives work as layered 'living immune systems', with antimicrobial defences built into the structure, the brood and the stored food. Lead with the layers: what kills microbes at each level of the hive. The why: colony collapse threatens crop pollination, and this shows habitat and hive materials, not only bees, protect a colony from disease. Name the journal and the team.

stories.label: US Moves to Bar DeepSeek From Federal Agencies and Contracts
stories.summary: The Trump administration ordered civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products and services and barred them from contracts. Lead with the reason given against the reason that matters: officials cite security, but DeepSeek's cheap open-weight models threaten Silicon Valley's pricing, and this is industrial policy as much as security policy. Explain how far the ban reaches (contractors, open weights run on US servers). WARNING to writer: only the Bloomberg link is about DeepSeek. The Economic Times and The Hill links in sources are about Musk's SpaceX share pledge, so do not use them.

stories.label: Paris Curfew, Protest Ban Announced As France Seeks To Restore Order
stories.summary: The new development since Macron's address: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has asked local authorities to impose partial curfews, Paris is banning protests and Marseille has banned public gatherings from noon to 8pm. Lead with the curfews and the ban. The mechanism is a government answering student-led unrest with emergency public-order powers, not concessions, after 2,397 detentions and the burning of Limoges town hall. Say who bears the restrictions: young people and the banlieues.

stories.label: Arrest Warrant Issued for Raúl Castro in the U.S. State of Florida
stories.summary: A Miami judge has signed a state first-degree murder warrant for Raúl Castro over the 1996 Brothers to the Rescue shootdown, on top of May's federal indictment. Lead with the new state charge. The mechanism is US domestic courts reaching a foreign former head of state, and after the Maduro precedent the question is whether a warrant becomes a pretext for force against Cuba. Note what immunity rules and Cuba's response say. Dateline Miami.

stories.label: Carney warns Alberta not to stumble into 'Brexit'
stories.summary: Albertans vote today in a referendum on independence from Canada, with Carney comparing it to Brexit and Saskatchewan separatists watching. Lead with the vote itself. The mechanism is an oil province's grievance over federal climate and pipeline policy becoming a sovereignty question. Say what a Yes would and would not trigger legally (the Clarity Act and the Supreme Court's 1998 Quebec reference), and note First Nations treaty claims on the land. Dateline Edmonton.

stories.label: India extends detention of top Cockroach Janta Party leaders
stories.summary: There are two new developments. A Delhi magistrate extended the custody of two CJP leaders, and Rediff contrasts this with bail granted to a murder convict. Activists of the Hindu Raksha Dal, a Sangh Parivar outfit, were filmed beating student protesters in Delhi (The Diplomat). Lead with the vigilante beatings alongside the state's detentions: the state jails protest leaders while aligned groups attack the rank and file. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Lithuania foils arson attempt on company storing Starlink equipment
stories.summary: Molotov cocktails were thrown at a Lithuanian firm storing Starlink terminals bound for Ukraine. The prime minister blames Russia, and it follows similar attacks in Bulgaria and Poland. Lead with the pattern: three NATO states, one supply chain. The mechanism is sabotage of the private logistics behind Ukraine's battlefield communications, a target cheaper to hit than military depots. This is a separate event from yesterday's drone debris near Kaunas. Dateline Kaunas.

stories.label: State security prosecution summons Mada Masr editor-in-chief for investigation
stories.summary: Egypt's Supreme State Security Prosecution has summoned Lina Attalah, editor of Mada Masr, for questioning on Wednesday in Case 9072/2026. The summons gives no charge, and it is the sixth case against the outlet in six years. Lead with the missing charge and the count. The mechanism is the open-ended state-security case used as a tool against Egypt's last major independent newsroom. The summons comes as Cairo weighs sending troops to Saudi Arabia, a decision Mada Masr has reported on. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Israel-Backed Palestinian Militias Terrorize Displaced Families in Gaza
stories.summary: Drop Site's ground reporting from Jabaliya: Israel-armed Palestinian militias are attacking displaced families who live near the expanding 'yellow line'. Lead with named victims and incidents. The mechanism is occupation by proxy: Israel pushes the line forward and outsources coercion to armed collaborators, which blurs accountability. Name the militias and their Israeli backing as reported. Dateline Gaza City.

stories.label: Russia strikes 28 critical energy facilities across Ukraine in latest wave of attacks, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Russian missiles and drones hit 28 substations and other energy facilities overnight, and 550,000 households lost power as heating season begins. Lead with the households. The mechanism is a pre-winter campaign against the grid meant to make civilians pay, and it mirrors Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries. Note who repairs the grid and with what equipment. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: How the gold boom is fuelling tree loss from Ghana to the Amazon
stories.summary: The war-driven rally in gold is paying for excavators in Ghana's forests and the Amazon. Gold drove more deforestation than any other mineral between 2001 and 2019. Name the series: gold. Lead with the price-to-chainsaw link. The mechanism is that high prices make illegal mining profitable enough to outrun enforcement, and refiners and the LBMA are accountable for the provenance of what they buy. Those who pay are communities facing mercury-poisoned rivers and lost farmland. Dateline Accra.

stories.label: Rubio pitches US business in Central Asia, says China ties need not suffer
stories.summary: In Samarkand, Washington and the five Central Asian states set out cooperation on critical minerals, transport and technology, and Rubio said they need not cut ties with China. Lead with the minerals. The mechanism is a US bid for Kazakh and Uzbek uranium, tungsten and rare earths, and for trade corridors that avoid Russia and Iran, in a region whose trade still runs through Beijing and Moscow. These are Muslim-majority states choosing between patrons. Dateline Samarkand.

stories.label: Bitcoin mining offshoot loses Microsoft AI deal as power delay stretches into 2030s
stories.summary: Microsoft walked away from Nscale's planned AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, because a grid connection won't come until the 2030s. Britain's data-centre connection requests now total about 73 gigawatts. Lead with the 73 GW queue. The mechanism is that electricity, not chips, is the binding constraint on AI build-outs, and it strands bitcoin miners who pivoted to AI on borrowed money. Dateline Loughton.

stories.label: Huge DMV data breach impacted current and former Florida residents
stories.summary: Florida's motor-vehicle agency is notifying victims of a ShinyHunters breach of driver's licence and vehicle records, but not everyone whose data was stolen is being told. Lead with the notification gap and the scale. The mechanism is a state database that every driver is forced to feed, held by an agency that owes them little disclosure, and it is the same gang behind this year's wave of SaaS data thefts. Dateline Tallahassee.

stories.label: 正面硬刚DeepSeek！MiniMax M3.1 Flash发布，输出卷到200+TPS，价格砍到1/2
stories.summary: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash, the anonymous 'Space Bunny' model that topped OpenRouter. It has a 1M-token context, runs at 200+ tokens per second, and costs ¥1 in and ¥4 out per million tokens, roughly half DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's peak price. It came 48 hours after DeepSeek's release and matches it on agent benchmarks. Lead with the price war: two Chinese labs are making near-flagship agentic coding cheap enough to undercut US frontier pricing. Benchmarks are self-reported; say so. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
stories.summary: An AI-generated proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis has been checked and unpacked by human mathematicians, unlike earlier AI proofs, and one calls the implications 'staggering'. Lead with what was proved and who verified it. The mechanism is the shift from AI as a search tool to AI producing proofs that humans then have to understand. Explain what the result says in plain terms and what remains open (the full Riemann hypothesis).

stories.label: We were looking at it wrong": The explosive claim that's upended the AI world
stories.summary: Goodfire researcher Nick Cammarata's 26,000-word post argues that neural networks are far less complicated inside than interpretability research assumed, and AI-safety researchers are treating it as good news. Lead with the claim in one sentence and the evidence behind it. The mechanism: if a model's internals are legible, auditing what a model will do becomes feasible. Include the sceptics and note that the work is not peer-reviewed. Dateline San Francisco.
